lines.trans: Look up at those four lines from the balcony—not one lantern twisted overnight!
And look down at the tables: twenty-eight linen napkins clipped tight with numbered birch pins!
Even Tariq clipped four extra clothespins to the corners of every white tablecloth!
At three this afternoon I bake four berry almond cakes so they are warm by six.
And at four this afternoon Suad and I finish rehearsing our four-hand piano duet!
Everything is timed to the minute: afternoon prep, five-thirty tea, six sharp arrival!
Knock on wood right now, Nour, whenever someone says everything is timed to the minute!
What could possibly change at noon? Our guest wrote six this evening in black ink!
Wait—do you two hear the front-desk telephone ringing through the lobby window?
That is a very loud, very urgent Saturday noon ring, Nour!
Even Tariq just looked up from his paper ledger behind the glass door!
Hold my apron—I had better answer that call before twelve chimes finish!

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Elative form of حسن (hasan), used for comparison.

examples.trans: This is the best room in the house.
I feel better today.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The color black.

examples.text: جيب لفة لزاق أسود من الدكان.
examples.trans: Pick up a roll of black tape from the shop.
The black cat is sleeping under the tree.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The reception desk is beside the door.
Thank you for the warm welcome.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'twelve'; before a singular counted noun it takes -r: اطنعشر دقة ('twelve chimes').

examples.trans: The clock tower chimed twelve!
Here is twelve dinars change.

meanings.note: The day of the week, Saturday.

examples.text: كل سبت الصبح بنمشي عسوق الحارة.
examples.trans: Every Saturday morning we walk to the neighbourhood market.

examples.text: الخبز الطازة بيجهز يوم السبت الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: Fresh bread is ready on Saturday at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Form VII passive of لف ('to wrap, turn'), common for parcels and fragile dishes.

examples.trans: The cups were wrapped well in newspaper.

examples.text: الخبز السخن ما بينلف بكيس مسكر.
examples.trans: Hot bread is not wrapped in a closed bag.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواب.

examples.trans: The wooden door is open now.
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Used as a material noun after خشب ('birch wood') or ملقط ('birch clothespin').

examples.trans: Birch wood is smooth and light in colour.
We have clean birch clothespins.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of حضّر ('to prepare'). Plural: تحضيرات.

examples.trans: Coffee prep takes ten minutes.
All preparations for the party are ready.

meanings.note: Core Levantine verb for 'look (at)' taking على or في.

examples.text: تطلعي من الشباك شوفي لون الشيش الأخضر!
examples.trans: Look out the window and see the green colour of the shutters!

examples.text: ليش بتطلعوا علي هيك؟ هلا بمسح الدهان!
examples.trans: Why are you staring at me like that? I'll wipe the paint right now!

meanings.note: Form V intransitive counterpart to غيّر ('to change something').

examples.trans: The appointment changed a moment ago.
The weather changes quickly in spring.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تليفونات.

examples.trans: The phone rang on the reception desk.
I wrote the phone number in the notebook.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of مرّن ('to train / practice'). Plural: تمارين.

examples.trans: We have piano rehearsal at four o'clock.
This exercise is easy and useful.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for berries/mulberries (singulative توتة 'one berry').

examples.trans: The berry and almond cake came out warm.
We bought fresh berries from the market.

meanings.note: Feminine plural جامدات also appears in Jordanian speech for firm fruit (متل ليمونات جامدات).

examples.text: نقي ليمونات صفر وجامدات عشان تارت الليمون.
examples.trans: Pick firm yellow lemons for the lemon tarts.

examples.text: الكريمة بردت بالبراد وصارت جامدة ومتماسكة.
examples.trans: The curd chilled in the fridge and turned firm and set.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic and colloquial term for ink used in pens.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in blue ink.
The ink pen is on the desk.

meanings.note: Used to mean 'even' (e.g., even he went) or 'until' (e.g., until tomorrow).

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Can mean a physical line, a phone line, a bus route, or handwriting.

examples.trans: Your handwriting on the card is clear and neat.
Stay with me on the line a second.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخلص, بيخلص).

examples.trans: I finished making the bed quickly!

examples.text: كل ما أخلص عزف كنا نحكي.
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, we used to chat.

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

خِلِص.gloss: to run out; be finished; end

meanings.en: to run out; be finished; end
meanings.note: Form I intransitive counterpart of transitive خلّص ('to finish something'): خلص الخبز means 'the bread has run out'.

examples.text: يلا نمشي قبل ما يخلص الخبز السخن.
examples.trans: Let's walk over before the hot bread sells out.

examples.text: خلصت القهوة، رح أعمل إبريق جديد.
examples.trans: The coffee ran out; I will make a fresh pot.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Past tense verb for knocking on a door, hammering a nail, or sometimes calling someone on the phone ('daqq 'ala').

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast!
The clock tower started chiming twelve.

meanings.note: Covers daqqa ('a knock / clock chime', pl. دقات) and diqqa ('precision / punctuality', الدقة بالمواعيد).

examples.text: سمعنا اطنعشر دقة من برج الساعة.
examples.trans: We heard twelve chimes from the clock tower.
I always love punctuality.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: روس.

examples.trans: My glasses were on my head!

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من السقف الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low ceiling.

meanings.note: Derived from أربعة ('four'). Used for four-hand piano pieces or four-sided shapes.

examples.trans: Our four-hand piano piece is ready.
The table has a four-sided shape.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برد, بيرد).

examples.text: اشربي شاي أول وبعدين ردي عالجرس.
examples.trans: Drink tea first and then answer the bell.
Nobody answered the phone at the station.

meanings.note: Standard verb for lifting something up or raising.

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
He raised his cup in a toast to the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برن, بيرن).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
The old wire always rings twice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رنات.

examples.trans: The doorbell gave a single ring.
I heard two quick rings from the buzzer.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'extra' (قطع زيادة extra pieces, الدرج الزيادة the extra stairs).

examples.trans: I brought two extra chairs for the courtyard.
I put a little extra mint in the tea.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Active participle of سمع ('to hear'), standard in Jordanian for 'can you hear?' (سامعني؟).

examples.trans: I hear you clearly on the phone.
Do you hear the sound of a car outside the gate?

meanings.note: Respectful and warm Levantine title for a woman ('Madam / Mrs. / lady').

examples.text: يسلموا إيديكي يا ست سعاد عاللحن الحلو.
examples.trans: Bless your hands, Madam Suad, for the lovely melody.

examples.text: كل ست وشيخ بالحارة معزومين عالافتتاح.
examples.trans: Every lady and elder on the lane is invited to the opening.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شراشف.

examples.trans: We spread a clean white cloth on the table.
I brought fresh sheets from the closet.

meanings.note: Standard feminine noun (plural شرفات) for a balcony or upper open terrace; everyday Amman speech also uses برندة or سطح.

examples.text: شربنا الشاي على الشرفة وقت الغروب.
examples.trans: We drank tea on the terrace at sunset.
We hung colourful lanterns on the upper rooftop terrace.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشبك, بيشبك).

examples.trans: Plug in Tariq's brass lamp.
We clipped the second sheet to the envelope.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation (duhur) for midday (12:00 p.m.).

examples.text: الكافيه بيقدم شوربة سخنة من الضهر للمسا.
examples.trans: The café serves hot soup from noon until evening.

examples.text: الشمس بتكون عالية ودافية وقت الضهر.
examples.trans: The sun is high and warm at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: ضيفة). Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Can refer to physical length, height, or duration of time (e.g., all day).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Can mean physically high or loud (for a voice or sound).

examples.trans: What is that loud sound upstairs?
The wooden ceiling is high and sunny.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Piano playing calms the nerves.
Whenever she finishes playing, she smiles.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصور.

examples.trans: We arrived at the guesthouse Monday afternoon.
Late-afternoon tea in the courtyard is a daily ritual.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فوط.

examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water.
She wiped the table with a damp cloth.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Masculine material noun used both for woven linen fabric and flax/linen twine.

examples.text: هاد المريول مصنوع من قماش الكتان البارد.
examples.trans: This apron is made from cool linen fabric.
Linen holds up well in summer and its heat.

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.text: ريحة اللوز المحمص طالعة من فرن سلمى.
examples.trans: The aroma of toasted almonds is drifting out of Salma's oven.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز بتعطي تارت الليمون قرمشة طيبة.
examples.trans: An almond crust gives the lemon tart a delicious crunch.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليالي.

examples.trans: The guest arrived last night.
The neighbourhood is very quiet at night.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مداخل.

examples.trans: The guesthouse entrance is lit by a brass lantern.
We greeted the guests at the entrance.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of رقّم ('to number'): feminine مرقمة, plural مرقمين.

examples.text: الأوراق مرقمة من واحد لعشرة بالترتيب.
examples.trans: The sheets are numbered from one to ten in order.
I found the numbered boxes next to the door.

meanings.note: Masculine Levantine noun (plural مراييل) worn while cooking, painting, or crafting.

examples.text: البس مريول الرسم قبل ما تفتح الألوان.
examples.trans: Put on the painting apron before you open the paints.
The apron got splashed all over with blue ink.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مستعجلة, plural: مستعجلين).

examples.trans: He was always in a hurry during music lessons.
Have some tea if you are not in a hurry.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسك, بيمسك).

examples.trans: Hold this torch steady right here.
Grab the boxes, Tariq!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مشبوكة, plural: مشبوكين).

examples.text: في صفحة تانية مشبوكة ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: There is a second page clipped behind the letter.
The lamp is plugged in.

meanings.note: Pronounced mazbuut in Amman; means 'properly, accurately, that's right!'.

examples.trans: Let me speak with him properly!
What you say is one hundred percent right.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مكالمات.

examples.trans: An important phone call came in on the landline.
She finished the call in two minutes.

meanings.note: Fine tweezers for delicate repair work, or small kitchen tongs.

examples.text: طارق طلب ملقط رفيع عشان يمسك الدبوس النحاس.
examples.trans: Tariq asked for thin tweezers to hold the tiny brass pin.

examples.text: البرغي الصغير ما بينمسك إلا بملقط.
examples.trans: That tiny screw can only be picked up with tweezers.

meanings.note: Used to ask for permission 'is it possible?' or to say 'perhaps'.

examples.trans: May I see the room first?
Could I see the tag in the sunlight?

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.en: arrival; reaching a place or time
meanings.note: Masculine verbal noun (masdar) of وصل ('to arrive/reach').

examples.text: لازم نخلص كل شي قبل وصول الضيوف.
examples.trans: We need to finish everything before the guests' arrival.
Thank God for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!
